doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Reflections on the life of a musician
title: The machine-gun owner and other funny stories
summary: Ware recounts the tramp band running from a tavern owner firing a machine gun, and a dog episode.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: When you think back, are there any highlights or any significant things that you haven't thought of that you didn't get a chance to mention? There's so much.

There's so much. It's hard to try to just pick something out, you know, to say. But I want to tell you something funny, though. In our hustling days, back there in the '30s, we went out with the tramp band one

night. We had this long -- we'd hired somebody with a touring car. I don't know, one of them old Buicks, had running board on it. We out there on, past Cicero, and one of them roadhouse taverns like -- one of the guys go in and ask the man, "Could we come in and play?" He says, "No, no, we don't want you in here." But the customers said, "Yeah, come on." So, we just struck up right there outside of the club and we're out there just playing our little Tiger Rag, (unintelligible), and the people clapping and putting money in our hat. The owner come out of the back door and he had a machine gun.
He started firing up in the air. We started running. Can you imagine me running with that big homemade fiddle? And the guy had the car, driving off.
People got more kicks out of that. But it was frightening. That's the kind of things we had to go through. You know, I can think of some hilarious scenes.
Now, they seem -- in retrospect, they seem funny. But having lived through those.
It's like (unintelligible) little tavern, doing our number. Here's a lady with a little dog and I think it was Phineas -- he's out in front doing the mugging and dancing --
Bill Henderson's older brother mounted his legs; (Unintelligible). He was dancing. This dog (unintelligible) growling.
